section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains two interpretations of the verse "Let the power of Ado-nai be great," one as drawing down the source of Ado-nai and the other as an increase within Ado-nai itself, linking it to the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy.
section.t: And the explanation of the matter in more particularity will be understood by prefacing the precise wording of the verse, "And now, let the power of Ado-nai be great, please,"
for there are two interpretations of this.
For in several discourses
it is explained that the interpretation of "let the power of Ado-nai be great" is that there should be drawn into Ado-nai its power
(the root and source of Ado-nai)
and through this there will be its greatness.
And the simple interpretation of "let the power of Ado-nai be great" is
(and so it is explained in several discourses)
that there should be a greatness
(also)
in the power of Ado-nai.
And based on this, one will understand
(more)
the connection of "let the power of Ado-nai be great, please" to "Hashem, slow to anger, etc."
(the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy that are above the chain of descent),
because in order for there to be the greatness in the power of Ado-nai
(the root and source of Ado-nai)
it is through the drawing down from a level that is above the chain of descent,
above even the root and source of the chain of descent.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the name Ado-nai corresponds to Malchus, and its power (root) is in Chochmah, illustrated by the analogy of speech letters whose source is in the hidden wisdom of the soul, which adds to the intellect when expressed.
section.t: And the matter is,
that the name Ado-nai is in Malchus
(as above),
and the power of Ado-nai
(the root and source of Malchus)
is in Chochmah,
for "Abba founded the daughter."
And this will be understood by way of analogy from the letters of speech in a person
(for Malchus in general is speech),
whose source
is above the light
(the intellect or the emotion)
that is clothed within them.
For the fact that the same rationale,
each one says it in different letters and words,
is because the source of the letters is from the level of Chochmah,
the hidden intellect and the primacy of the intellect
that is in the soul,
which is above the revealed intellect.
And this is the reason that by bringing the intellect into speech, there is an addition in the intellect beyond what it was initially
(in thought),
for through speech, there is drawn from the level of Chochmah, the root and source of the intellect.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the source of speech in Chochmah affects not only speech itself but also the intellect and emotions clothed within it, causing them to divide into many parts through the drawing of the primacy of the intellect.
section.t: And behold, this that the source of speech is in Chochmah is not only regarding the speech itself,
but also regarding the intellect and emotions that are clothed in the speech.
For through their being clothed in speech,
they become divided into many parts.
For when one speaks words of love,
the love in itself is one emotion,
and when it is clothed in the letters and words of speech, it is divided into several words,
each word containing a part of the emotion.
And similarly, when one speaks some intellectual rationale,
the rationale is one rationale,
and when it is clothed in the letters and words of speech, it is divided into several parts.
And this that the intellect and emotions come to division
(even though in themselves they are simple)
is because there is drawn into them from the level of Chochmah,
the primacy of the intellect.
